review: Second behavioral review; no external conviction used

samples.marker_line: Route-B loader: concealed archive launch; hide and self-delete traits
ltidisafe 1.7.3: silent preinstall exports host and user identity

members.identification: NetworkSpeedCheck bandwidth library; caller-selected HTTP/HTTPS endpoints and random upload data
Load-time OS identity exporter disguised as a download-speed test
ltidisafe 1.7.3 manifest activating the bundled exporter with silent npm preinstall

powershell: A constant 704123 is added to negative array integers and the result is invoked via ScriptBlock.Create().Invoke().
Decoded stage obtains its console handle, calls ShowWindow(handle,0), and moves it offscreen to (-10000,-10000) with zero size.
Creates a GUID-named TEMP directory and downloads a 7z archive plus a 7zr executable.
Checks archive magic and extractor MZ prefix/size, not authenticity.
Runs passworded extraction hidden, reads an extracted text password, extracts a nested archive, then selects an executable other than the extractor and starts it hidden.
Attempts Remove-Item against an environment variable assigned MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path. The dynamic script reassigns that variable; successful self-deletion is not established.
npm: Manifest identity is ltidisafe 1.7.3; the archive has exactly package.json, index.js, and test.js.
preinstall runs node test.js with stdout and stderr suppressed.
index.js implements HTTP/HTTPS download and upload speed measurement; no identity collection in this library.
test.js UTF-8 hex-encodes username, hostname and home directory, constructs a separate Oastify HTTP destination for each, and supplies it to the real download-speed method.
A QuickJS replay of the two original JavaScript files with mocked OS/HTTP/URL/Buffer modules captured exactly three GETs. Hex labels decode to reviewer, review-host, and /home/reviewer.
Interface IPv4 addresses are enumerated into localip but never transmitted. Uptime calls are comments.

judgment_basis.powershell: Concealed executable staging, nested password extraction, hidden launch, and cleanup outweigh an unidentified legitimate purpose. No final payload behavior or family attribution is assumed.
judgment_basis.npm: Silent install-time user and host disclosure to a hardcoded callback service is unrelated to the exported bandwidth API. An authorized registry security test is conceivable, but no consent or opt-in context is present.

trait_design: Notable atoms describe encoded source syntax/relationships. Hostile composites additionally require the existing concealed archive payload chain. Original console-control and environment-path cleanup findings remain unchanged.
matcher_limits: Compact arrays with uniform four through nine digit negative magnitudes, source at most 256 KiB, identifier length one through 64.
Self-path binding requires the same identifier spelling in a cleartext environment assignment and the encoded removal; it does not prove runtime deletion success.
Source-token relationships do not establish general execution reachability or payload behavior.
Some Node flow projections are limited; manual tracing and an entirely mocked replay establish the original source-to-request path.

coverage_goal.powershell: Three hostile behaviors now covered: concealed payload launch, window concealment and attempted self-deletion. Existing suspicious detections preserved.
coverage_goal.npm: Two hostile detections cover the one supported hostile behavior (identity export) and its preinstall packaging. The complete three-member archive was traced. Install activation, redirection, hex conversion and interface enumeration have accurate notable coverage. No additional distinct hostile operation was found; IP exfiltration, persistence, execution of remote code and credential theft are unsupported, so no extra hostile rules were invented.

remaining_disagreements: Classifier v18.18 emits BENIGN for the malicious npm archive and its exfiltration script despite retained hostile rules; the scan also warns that its feature specification v18 predates expected v21.
